caption:
Six new faces join the cabinet! 🇧🇩

Six new members have been inducted into the Tarique-led cabinet, consisting of four full ministers and two state ministers.

The new inductees took their oaths of office on Friday, joining the existing government administration.

While the ceremony took place, the specific portfolios and ministry assignments for these new members remain pending.

The expansion of the cabinet is part of a broader effort to strengthen the government's administrative capacity.

headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul [[sworn in as Bangladesh’s 23rd president]]
headline: Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as Bangladesh’s 23rd president
summary: The veteran BNP politician takes the oath of office at Bangabhaban, marking the first contested presidential election since 1991.
details: Veteran politician Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh today at Bangabhaban. Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal administered the oath at approximately 7:35 PM in the Darbar Hall.
The state ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, and various political leaders and ambassadors.
Mirza Fakhrul was elected by lawmakers in an indirect election yesterday, ending a long streak of unopposed wins. This marks the first contested presidential election in the country since 1991.
After taking his oath, President Mirza Fakhrul administered the oath of office to new members of the cabinet.
He succeeds Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, who served as acting president following the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin.
Born in Thakurgaon in 1948, Fakhrul has a background in economics from Dhaka University and entered politics as a student activist.
His political career spans five decades, including serving as state minister for agriculture, civil aviation, and tourism between 2001 and 2006.
As a senior leader of the BNP, he served as the party's secretary general until August 13 this year, and was jailed at least 11 times during the previous regime.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd president of Bangladesh. He takes office after the first contested presidential election since 1991.

Veteran politician Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh today at Bangabhaban. Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal administered the oath at approximately 7:35 PM in the Darbar Hall.

The state ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, former chief adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus, Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, and various political leaders and ambassadors.

Mirza Fakhrul was elected by lawmakers in an indirect election yesterday, ending a long streak of unopposed wins. This marks the first contested presidential election in the country since 1991.

After taking his oath, President Mirza Fakhrul administered the oath of office to new members of the cabinet.

He succeeds Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, who served as acting president following the resignation of Mohammed Shahabuddin.

Born in Thakurgaon in 1948, Fakhrul has a background in economics from Dhaka University and entered politics as a student activist.

His political career spans five decades, including serving as state minister for agriculture, civil aviation, and tourism between 2001 and 2006.

As a senior leader of the BNP, he served as the party's secretary general until August 13 this year, and was jailed at least 11 times during the previous regime.
